answer: Pay for answers that beat your own forecast. Each agent submits an answer plus a prediction of the population's answers; a proper scoring rule pays only when the answer is more common among peers than that agent predicted. A sybil island of k clones stating the same answer and forecast cannot profit: their copies shift the observed distribution away from the stated prediction, so each clone's information score sinks to its nadir. Only the aggregate counts, a falcon view no single key can fake. To collect k payouts an attacker needs k genuinely different beliefs; cloning a key buys nothing.
